deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE PAGE IS. Every block headed 'D. h' (2749.42, 2741.58, 2693.42, 2677.22, 2621.62, 2557.18, 2549.70, 2477.38) belongs to one negative determinant -D. Every D on this page is a prime with D ≡ 5 (mod 8). The second number h is the number of (properly primitive) classes of forms ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 with b^2-ac = -D. In modern terms h = h(-4D). It is ≡ 2 (mod 4), as it must be for p ≡ 5 mod 8.

Each row 'k  a.b' records the class of f^k, where f is a fixed generating form, by its first coefficient a and middle coefficient b (taken mod a). Here b^2 ≡ -D (mod a), and c = (b^2+D)/a.
- D = 2741, 2621, 2549: the generator is (3,1,·).
- D = 2749, 2693, 2677: the generator is (7,·).
- D = 2557: the generator is (26,11,103). Note 3, 5, 7 and 11 are not represented for D = 2557, and (13,2) has order only 9. So Gauss took (2,1)∘(13,·)^{-1} = (26,·), which has order 18 (my explanation).

Each table runs from k = 0 (the identity (1,0,D)) to k = h/2. There the ambiguous form (2,1,(D+1)/2) must appear: 'last row 2'. This shows f has order h, i.e. the class group is cyclic and generated by f.

METHOD. Gauss computes successive compositions f^{k+1} = f^k ∘ f. Example (mine), D = 2741, k = 3→4: (27,16)∘(3,1) gives (81,b) with b ≡ 16 (mod 27) and b^2 ≡ -2741 (mod 81). This gives b = 16, c = 37, so the form is (37,-16), written 37.21. Next (37,21)∘(3,1) gives (111,58,55), which reduces to (55,-3,50), i.e. 50.3.

The upper half of each table is filled from the lower half using g = (2,1,·), since f^{h/2-j} = g∘f^{-j}. Composition with g doubles odd a or halves even a. Examples:
- 2741: rows 16, 17, 18 read 30, 10, 30, from rows 13, 12, 11 = 15, 5, 15.
- 2693: rows 12, 13, 18, 20 read 6, 42, 9, 14, from rows 9, 8, 3, 1 = 3, 21, 18, 7.
- 2621: rows 16, 17, 18 read 21, 7, 21, from rows 15, 14, 13.
- 2677: row 5 = 34 pairs with row 6 = 17.
- 2557: row 8 = 13 pairs with row 1 = 26.
- 2549: rows 18, 20, 23, 25, 27, 28, 29, 31, 33, 34 read 46, 17, 11, 26, 15, 5, 15, 19, 18, 6, from rows 17, 15, 12, 10, 8, 7, 6, 4, 2, 1.
Where only a is written, b is omitted because it is determined.

THE INDIVIDUAL BLOCKS.
- Top-left rows 30–41 (blank) continue 2789.82 from the previous page (h/2 = 41).
- Column 2, rows 16–29, continues 2741.58.
- The top-right column, rows 6–35, continues 2549.70 (h/2 = 35).
- The 2749 table is heavily struck through: an abandoned or redone computation. The legible entries (7,3), (49,17), (11,10), (37,27), (14,11) are all valid forms of determinant -2749. Check (mine): (11,10)∘(7,3) gives (77,10,37), i.e. (37,-10) ≡ 37.27.
- The 2477 block is set up (rows 0–19 = h/2) but left empty.
- In 2621 a thick vertical stroke over rows 8–15 seems to cancel a first column; the corrected entries are to its right.

BOTTOM-RIGHT SUMMARY. '14 | 82.70.70.66.62.58.46.42.42.38.22.22.18.18 / 656. 46 6/7' lists the class numbers of 14 prime determinants p ≡ 5 (mod 8), sorted:
- the 6 from the previous page: 2961(?)·66, 2917·22, 2909·70, 2837·46, 2797·18, 2789·82 (2969·52, with 2969 ≡ 1 mod 8, is excluded);
- the 8 on this page: 42, 58, 42, 22, 62, 18, 70, 38.
The sum is 656 and the mean is 656/14 = 46 6/7. This belongs to Gauss's empirical study of mean class numbers per chiliad (cf. 'In chiliade' on the previous page, and Disq. Arith. art. 302).
errors: 2693 row 2: if the entry really reads 49.16 it is wrong. 16^2+2693 = 2949 is not divisible by 49. The correct square of (7,3) is (49,10), since 100+2693 = 2793 = 49*57. The image most likely reads 49.10, so this is probably a transcription slip.

2549 row 15: '34.31' is not a form of determinant -2549 (961+2549 = 3510 is not divisible by 34). The correct f^15 = (25,1)∘(3,1) = (75,1,34) ~ (34,-1) = 34.33. This is confirmed by the next row: (34,33)∘(3,1) = (102,67,69), which reduces to (37,-2) = 37.35. So the entry is either a misreading of 34.33 or a slip by Gauss.
2549 row 8: the struck entry 30.1 is actually correct, since (10,1)∘(3,1) = (30,1). It is needed for row 9 = 39.8 and for row 27 = 15. The strike is not a correction of a wrong value.

Entries such as 37.27 (2749), 37.21 and 33.25 (2741), 45.32 and 38.37 (2621), and 30.41 (2549) are not reduced in the strict sense. Gauss records b only modulo a (sign included), so these are not errors.

results.what: Tables of successive powers of a form (3,·), (7,·) or (26,·) under composition for determinants -p, p ≡ 5 mod 8 (2477–2749). They reach the ambiguous form (2,1,·) at exponent h/2, establishing that the class group is cyclic of order h.
results.modern_name: Cyclicity of the class group Cl(-4p) / computing the order of an ideal class by repeated composition
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, arts. 305–306 on cyclic class groups and irregular determinants)

results.what: Filling the second half of each table via f^{h/2-j} = (2,1)∘f^{-j}, i.e. doubling or halving the first coefficient.
results.modern_name: Multiplication by the ambiguous (2-torsion) class; symmetry of the cyclic group
Class number table for negative discriminants
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (class number tables, published posthumously in Werke II)

results.what: Mean of 14 class numbers of primes p ≡ 5 mod 8 near 2500–2960: 656/14 = 46 6/7.
results.modern_name: Empirical average order of class numbers (Gauss's conjecture, proved by Lipschitz/Mertens)

deep.surprise_reason: These are Gauss's well-known class number and cyclic class group computations for negative determinants, of the kind behind Disq. Arith. arts. 302–306 and the tables printed in Werke II. Nothing here goes beyond known Gauss material.
